newsitem.title: INDIA: India police orders leader's arrest in graft case.
newsitem.headline: India police orders leader's arrest in graft case.

text.p: India's federal police ordered the arrest of a leading politician at the centre of a corruption scandal on Tuesday after the Supreme Court dismissed his appeal for legal protection against detention.

Laloo Prasad Yadav resigned last Friday as chief minister of Bihar state soon after a special court issued a warrant for his arrest in a case which has rattled Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's coalition and sparked a debate on corruption.

The nation's highest court rejected on Tuesday an appeal by Yadav against a state court's order refusing to grant him "anticipatory bail", allowed under Indian law to people expecting possible arrest.

"We are in complete agreement with the High Court on the question of anticipatory bail," a three-judge bench of the Supreme Court ruled. "We reject the petition by the appellant against the High Court judgment."

Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) Director R.C. Sharma ordered officials in the state capital of Patna to carry out the warrants against Yadav and three other politicians involved in the scandal, official sources said in New Delhi.
The CBI named 56 politicians and officials in the $280-million scandal involving alleged embezzlement of animal welfare funds in India's second most populous state.
Yadav, who was indicted by the the CBI in April for his links to the so-called "fodder" scandal, named his wife Rabri Devi, a housewife, as his successor immediately after resigning on Friday.
The CBI says Yadav must be arrested to prevent any tampering with evidence in the case.
Yadav, a charismatic low-caste leader, says he is innocent. For months he resisted calls from opposition parties and allies to resign and face trial.

Devi easily won a confidence vote in the Bihar state assembly on Monday, but her appointment angered opposition parties and posed a challenge to the credibility of Gujral's 15-party United Front alliance.

The alliance decided on Friday not to admit Yadav's Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) group into its fold, but Gujral has faced criticism for not acting earlier to remove Yadav, a former party ally of Gujral.
The 38-year-old Devi, who has not studied beyond primary school, is viewed by opposition parties as a desperate attempt by Yadav to retain political influence.
On Tuesday, Devi formed a cabinet of 74 ministers, although her RJD party has only 136 members in the 324-seat state assembly.
"Such a huge ministry will cause a great burden on the state exchequer which is already in peril," said Sushil Kumar Modi, leader of the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
Devi enlisted support from the Congress party and regional groups demanding a separate Jharkhand province carved out of Bihar to win the vote of confidence on Monday.
